prs.title: Bound the deferred six-recipient repair for owned 1551
prs.body:
## Change and mathematical scope

**NO VERIFIED GAIN.** On exact [#7481](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7481) at `89eaa9d8cae37c1540de98f2d29a3abaabb96a2b`, two fixed chart-127 repair interfaces cannot recover the historical role-862 operand after deferring the six owned1551 updates.

- Before ADD46149, x230=−1 and x547=1 kill four named carriers and edited recipient873 while the old source is −1.
- Before ADD47956, the first outward deadline across all six recipients, a new exact 20-coordinate input kills all 644 edited chart-127 rows while the old source is −2. Independent literal replay checks both prefixes, all 73 INIT/COPY guards in each trace, and the signed changes to all six recipients. The earlier probe leaves 284 nonzero responses at this later cut.

Deleting the rank-four MOVE has optimistic gross about 67.657064563108 raw before repair. No literal edit survives either fixed interface. κ stays unchanged.

## Task and overlap

Refine the fixed-paid repair scope for the complex supplier on canonical base `e54523517d0f03e58352e647c403a5af3e525a57`, with signed [#7113](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7113) at `07a76c5e2738882c0cb322278e56f6cae3c9885d`. [#7491](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7491) treats one outward ADD on the original chart, while this scope changes the first repair to chart127 for six recipients. The two separate CI prerequisites reuse [#7257](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7257).

## Validation

From a clean POSIX checkout with CPython 3.12:

```sh
python3.12 -I -B research/p104-owned1551-fanout-banks/replay.py
```

The wrapper authenticates the exact source inputs, regenerates both separators and the directed price, and checks altered-input and wrong-response controls. It preserves the original capped receipt as provenance. Direct and registered replay, commit modes and source-history checks, read-only Git-free export and 27 onboarding tests passed locally. Neither cut reached a literal construction or physical replay.

## Credit

[#7491](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7491) supplies the single-recipient receiver-bank method. [#7003](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7003) supplies old-source timing, #7481/#7480/#7334 the exact native lineage, #7113 the signed caller, #7482/#7298 the coefficient and directed-price tools, and #7499 public copies of the pinned inputs. OpenAI Codex and subagents materially assisted proof, implementation, independent replay and packaging. Review and merge remain with maintainers.

## Open next questions

Other repair times, earlier encodings and changed paid routes remain open. A different route must carry the historical operand before the first outward read and restore all six independent returns at positive full price.

prs.title: Share the literal phase/egress boundary on 20 tapes (no κ)
prs.body:
## Summary

Reduce the supplied literal phase/egress boundary from 36 physical tapes to **20**, including two public owners. This scoped constructive proof answers CubeJerry #7425's explicit shared-bank question. The existing component arithmetic and successful retirement are cited premises, not audit deliverables. The new shared graph and composition proof were produced by Nick Petalas.

```text
same twenty tape identities:
  entry 17814: literal input phase; return
  supplied exact C and format service, outside this graph
  entry 0: literal egress; fixed jump; literal final phase; return
```

The fixed graph has 19,960 locations. All sixteen egress private roles share the phase bank after successful retirement. Head return, original DATA ownership and all historical backing remain charged. The exit costs exactly the sum of the original egress and final-phase instruction counts. This improves an inventory upper bound; it claims neither a global tape minimum nor lower total visited space. No new kappa or selected-frontier change.

Only `research/shared-phase-egress-bank/` is added, from canonical main `e54523517d0f03e58352e647c403a5af3e525a57`. The `formal-interface-lemma` card is explicitly changed to this supplied physical-boundary result. Exact pending-source bytes and original notices are retained locally with SHA256/Git-blob pins; replay needs no predecessor verification suite, remote fetch or unmerged Git object. [Advance claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19591459).

## Evidence

- Before: #7425's direct wrapper allocates 18 phase-private and 16 separate egress-private tapes plus two public tapes, for 36.
- After: the new two-entry graph passes 19 joined calls, 378 Gaussian coefficients and 1,297,236 literal instructions on the same twenty objects. It checks values, all heads, private erasure, opaque exterior, old-tail cleanup, all sixteen shared roles and historical unions across growing/shrinking packets. Five rejecting controls cover bad jumps, nonliteral opcodes, physical aliasing, exhausted execution budget and an omitted final phase.
- Warning-strict normal and optimized CPython 3.12.15 receipts agree exactly. The two registered commands took 0.1973 and 0.2182 seconds locally. These are check durations, not speedup claims. Registered replay, metadata/source pins, committed bytes/modes/source history, official export integrity and both read-only Git-free exported replays with empty PATH pass. Exported files remain unchanged. The direct marker is `PASS_SHARED_PHASE_EGRESS_BANK`.

From the repository root:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -B -W error research/shared-phase-egress-bank/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -O -B -W error research/shared-phase-egress-bank/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/shared-phase-egress-bank
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/shared-phase-egress-bank --check-source-history --check-modes
```

Another machine may substitute its CPython 3.12 path. The verifier prints a generated receipt bound to package and graph hashes. `PROOF.md` gives the unbounded composition argument; finite fixtures corroborate it.

## Limitations

Both routines require supplied blank private windows covering their combined visits. A larger invocation needs blankness of newly visited cells. This does not merge two arbitrary dirty banks. Rejection/interruption cleanup and rollback are unclaimed; the final phase retains its signed-range condition. The exact C producer, common-grid format conversion, source acquisition, caller allocation and their costs remain additional obligations. Test C production is an explicit outside oracle. No selected cold replay, full supplier, complete multiplier, independent human review or proof-kernel acceptance is claimed.

## Open next questions

Bind one actual C producer to the same header, address order, common grid, signed headroom and retired shared bank, and price its format conversion and allocation. Begin with one pinned caller occurrence. Further tape reduction requires changing simultaneous component liveness; this proof supplies no such construction or lower bound.

## Related open work

- #7425 supplies the literal outer phase, direct 36-tape wrapper and shared-bank question. This adds the twenty-tape graph and its successful-lifetime composition proof.
- #7422 supplies the retained literal normalization/egress and its numerical/retirement theorem. Its arithmetic and graph remain unchanged.
- #7477 adds rejection retirement to a whole-record reversal, a different failure contract. This construction uses no result or executable from it.

Credit CubeJerry / Jerry Chen, Ali Romman #5375, Tekalign #3127, Jose Manuel #2287 and #3087/#3091/#3098, JoyboyBrian #5329, Cinna Davis and Ryanson Jonathan #4325, the upstream stream/layer authors and all unchanged source notices. Lifetime sharing is elementary; the source-specific graph, proof and evidence are the contribution.

## CI notes

CI pending. Local package checks passed at `82d677390993e28e12a0203169a69d9d929aa5a2`; no hosted certification is claimed.

## Merge Danger

Door: two-way. Blast radius: one isolated research package. Shared code, predecessor files and selected records are unchanged.

prs.title: Classify all 15,710 surviving ordered column-plane parity cores (no κ)
prs.body:
## Summary

Answer Open next question 1 of unpaidmoon's #7282 with an exact duplicate-pair deletion criterion for two binary column planes.

```text
joint-type multiplicities
  -> odd-multiplicity support
  -> six distance inequalities + one rank-four test
  -> 15,710 surviving ordered coordinate orbits
```

**Scoped written proof:** deletion order is irrelevant; the tests are necessary and sufficient; a valid final core makes every intermediate deletion safe. The maximum used support is sharply seventeen coordinates. An exact multiplicity normal form covers all original pairs that survive complete deletion.

**Exact finite certificate:** all 524,288 type-labeled core states are enumerated, 467,945 are valid, and the 36 plane-basis changes give 15,710 ordered coordinate orbits. The order of the distinguished columns is preserved. The direct orbit count and a separate literal-matrix Burnside count agree at every support width.

The contribution was produced by Nick Petalas. Credit unpaidmoon for #7282's model and deletion question, retaining its #7221/#7139 and earlier image-space lineage. Its exact README and proof at `77b12ac33472b168c5ca6353572d76ed9a76e808` are committed unchanged with SHA256 and Git blob bindings. No predecessor scientific verifier is imported or replayed. Parity reduction, generator-matrix types, the binary simplex code and Burnside's lemma are classical methods.

Card `bit-new-register-model` is explicitly marked changed scope to this local binary geometry question. Selected #7000 and kappa remain unchanged.

## Evidence

- **Before:** #7282 leaves duplicate-pair deletion open beyond its examples and weight-two census.
- **After:** PROOF.md gives the all-multiplicity criterion and reduction; the new checker independently compares literal binary matrices with the criterion on the complete finite domain, then checks the orbit counts by two methods.
- Normal and optimized warning-strict direct runs passed on CPython 3.12.15, macOS 27.0.1 arm64, in 9.66 and 9.69 seconds respectively. These are single local check durations, not performance comparisons.
- Both registered VERIFY.json commands passed, with a 19.84-second total registered replay. Each command has a 120-second timeout. The checks include 1,200 literal deletion fixtures and separate rank, distance, cross-bit and collapse controls.
- Metadata/source pins and exact committed bytes/source history passed. Selected orientation returned PASS_RESEARCH_BASELINE_BINDINGS_ONLY and was not used as a scientific replay.

Exact reproduction from the repository root:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -W error -B research/column-plane-parity-core/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -W error -O -B research/column-plane-parity-core/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/column-plane-parity-core
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/column-plane-parity-core --check-source-history
```

On another machine substitute its CPython 3.12 executable. No third-party dependencies are needed. Both modes print PASS_COLUMN_PLANE_PARITY_CORE, with states_checked 524288, labeled_total 467945 and orbit_total 15710.

## Limitations

The all-width statements are written proofs; the orbit numbers are finite computational evidence. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed. No physical query word, native implementation, supplier admission, improved kappa or complete multiplication theorem is supplied. Lean, Docker and the selected scientific cold replay were not run. Unequal-type deletion, deletion of distinguished columns and exchange of the ordered planes are outside this contract.

Overlap checks included live handoffs/open PRs, account history, canonical-main searches and merged-PR searches for the object, general type model and exact quantities. The broad overlap corpus covered 800 open PRs and 7,400 Discussion records. Closed-corpus refresh timed out and sparse local note coverage was incomplete; direct main and merged searches supplemented those gaps. No absence of a match is treated as proof of novelty.

## Open next questions

- Price one surviving six-coordinate core under an explicit arbitrary-input native alphabet and complete producer/consumer/restoration bill. The present geometry gives no paid saving.
- Specify and test a changed deletion or replacement operation on the valid even-multiplicity example whose parity core collapses. New rank, distance, restoration and cost arguments are required.

## Related open work

- #7282 supplies the column-column model, earlier orbit results and the deletion question answered here; its numerical census is not this ordered parity-core census.
- #7221 supplies further dimension-six coordinate classes and motivates the wider classification; this result classifies survival under one explicit deletion rule.
- #7139 studies the total-image bound at pattern dimension four and its representative geometries; this contribution concerns duplicate-coordinate reduction of the column-column geometry.
- #7138 studies the weight-one no-edge image bound and a reducible column witness; this contribution does not re-establish or alter that bound.

prs.title: Prove the selected tensor phase needs exactly f+1 linear observations (no κ)
prs.body:
## Summary

Prove that the absolute diagonal phase of selected MOVE24472's right monomial needs exactly **f+1 binary affine-linear observations** for every positive tensor column count f, even when observations mix columns arbitrarily. Claim type: scoped written proof with exact finite corroboration.

```text
r_j = XOR of coordinates {0,1,2,3,5,6} in column j
b   = XOR of coordinate 7 across all columns
Q_f = f + 3 sum_j r_j + 2b modulo 4
translation periods: every r_j = 0 and b = 0
```

The period subgroup has dimension 8f-1. A sufficient linear statistic must have its kernel inside that subgroup, giving the matching f+1 lower bound. The joint statistic saves f-1 observation bits against retaining the two natural parities separately in every column. This is an information bound, not a physical storage claim; nonlinear evaluation of Q_f itself has a two-bit output.

Produced by Nick Petalas. Credit CubeJerry / Jerry Chen #7426, head `172f4535ce8dcff79f626410af845f757c1563be`, for the recipe, source binding, literal implementation **and the existing one-column parity contraction**. Only the complete tensor period subgroup and sharp observation minimum are new. Retain Ali Romman #5375, #7000's native/Gaussian lineage and Dennys / antunishdPursuit #6500's parity-expansion context. The general parity and quotient principles are classical. No predecessor executable was audited or replayed.

Only `research/selected-phase-linear-statistic/` is added. Base `e54523517d0f03e58352e647c403a5af3e525a57`, priority revision 8, selected #7000 unchanged. The formal-interface-lemma card explicitly changes scope to this written phase-information result. The [advance CLAIM](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19591467) predicted the f+1 bound; the [progress clarification](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19591585) credits the contraction already present in the predecessor's full proof.

## Evidence

- Before: the supplied recipe has a known contracted one-column phase, without a sharp all-column linear-observation minimum. After: an explicit joint statistic and a written all-f matching lower bound.
- `PASS_SELECTED_PHASE_LINEAR_STATISTIC`: every 512 one-column and 262,144 two-column address matches a separate literal strict-upper polynomial oracle. All 262,144 one-column derivative comparisons find 128 periods; constant derivatives classify every 262,144 two-column shift and find 32,768 periods. This uses independent column inputs, not 2^36 pairwise comparisons.
- Every one of 512 one-bit linear maps fails on its actual one-column fibers. A further 1,024 deterministic tensor fixtures at f=1..64, 3,072 Gaussian forward/inverse pairs, seven semantic negative controls, one positive cancellation control and five domain controls pass. Larger fixtures are not exhaustive.
- CPython 3.12.15, macOS arm64, standard library only. Both registered warning-strict normal/optimized commands pass locally, timed at about 0.70 seconds each. Generated receipts bind all seven package files and agree between modes. Registered replay, AST/compile inspection and committed bytes/modes/source-history preflight pass. Official export integrity and both read-only Git-free exported replays pass, leaving all eight export files unchanged. No local registered check is deferred to CI.

From the repository root, another CPython 3.12 path may replace this interpreter:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -B research/selected-phase-linear-statistic/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -O -B research/selected-phase-linear-statistic/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/selected-phase-linear-statistic
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/selected-phase-linear-statistic --check-source-history --check-modes
```

The exported factual recipe is byte-identical to the cited predecessor file, SHA256 `96fadb44c3316be93c6c02f50cd2c841a9541d67b98fd94fc47b73fa64dd404c`. Its original source binding is a cited premise. The direct checker needs neither a pending Git object nor network access.

## Limitations and unrun obligations

The theorem concerns fixed affine-linear observations followed by arbitrary decoding of this exact absolute phase. It is not a general circuit minimum or a nonlinear streaming-space lower bound. Acquisition, decoding, dirty restoration, movement/layout, owner return, signed range, historical backing and the complete paid invoice remain unpriced. It supplies no physical tape/runtime reduction, supplier admission, new kappa or complete multiplication theorem. All five selected framework assumptions remain. No selected scientific cold replay, predecessor suite, Lean, Docker, independent human review or formal-kernel verification was run.

## Open next questions

- Implement the contraction in one supplied literal phase producer and charge every parity read, carry, cleanup and retained backing before quoting physical savings.
- Specify a reversible sequential scan computing the nonlinear two-bit phase without retaining all f linear observations. The present decoder is mathematical, with no priced streaming contract.

This contribution stops at the first new proved information bound and reserves no follow-up.

## Related open work

- #7426 supplies the same diagonal phase and its existing one-column contraction. This adds the tensor period subgroup and sharp linear-observation rank, without replaying its machine.
- #7428 produces translation descriptors for the same native MOVE. Its physical producer/return contract is a separate composition obligation.
- #7430 implements that MOVE's binary address maps. This theorem concerns the diagonal phase and does not change those maps.
- #7429 implements the positive central C leaf of the same MOVE. Its integral-prefix and signed-range contracts remain separate.
- #7462 shortens that MOVE's left CNOT word. This computes no new address word or competing CNOT count.
- #7468 proves endpoint-promised integral prefix scales for the central tensor. This computes no competing scale.
- #7477 adds rejection retirement for the related record-reversal service. It does not supply this phase statistic or its physical producer.
- The active [variable-dimension quadratic-phase producer claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19591502) studies a streaming operation bill, while this proves a linear-information minimum. It is not a dependency; no cost number is compared.
